thread:
ravi: Noticed two prod-like staging restores failing during decrypt. Error from restore-agent: "AccessDenied: KMS failed to decrypt chunk: UnauthorizedOperation". Anyone touching key policies or service accounts overnight?

tessa: Which key? did the audit pipeline for IAM changes flag anything?

ravi: Key arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:222333444555:key/def-456-uvw. Audit shows a role rename in infra team (PR infra/rename-serviceacct) at 02:10UTC but no direct key-policy edits.

sec-bot: [alert] 2025-01-12T02:15:00Z - kms-grant-check - grantMismatchDetected key=def-456-uvw grantId=G-101010 grantee=arn:aws:iam::222333444555:role/old-data-uploader

chris: That alignes. Our grant-rotator relies on grantee ARN exact-match; when the role was renamed the rotator attempted to create a new grant but CreateGrant failed. See cloudtrail: `errorCode=InvalidPrincipalException message=Principal arn:aws:iam::222333444555:role/new-data-uploader does not exist` at 02:12UTC.

ravi: I pulled list-grants: ```
$ aws kms list-grants --key-id def-456-uvw --region us-east-1
Grants:
- GrantId: G-101010
  GranteePrincipal: arn:aws:iam::222333444555:role/old-data-uploader
  Operations: [Decrypt]
- GrantId: G-101011
  GranteePrincipal: arn:aws:iam::222333444555:role/enc-ops
```

ops-runner: Quick remediation: create a temp grant for the new role and run the restore. I can do that if sec approves.

chris: Before creating, double-check that new role has the expected assume-role trust for the uploader CI. Also confirm we don't have cross-account principal aliases that confuse grants.

sec-bot: Policy note: Creating grants for roles requires that the role is a principal in the account and not an assumed-role session. Confirm grantee is the role ARN, not a federated user.

tessa: I'm going to validate role existence: `aws iam get-role --role-name new-data-uploader` returns 200 OK. Role exists. The CreateGrant failures were from the rotator run before the rename completed across regions.

ravi: Ok making temp grant now:```
aws kms create-grant --key-id def-456-uvw --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::222333444555:role/new-data-uploader --operations Decrypt --name "temp-restore-grant" --region us-east-1
```
Created GrantId G-202020 expiry=2025-01-12T04:00:00Z

ops-runner: Running restore smoke: `./tools/snap-restore --env=staging --snap=snap-20250110`
ops-runner: restore log: `2025-01-12T02:38:45Z INFO decrypt part-0001: ok; part-0002: ok; restore complete` :white_check_mark:

chris: Nice. Root cause: timing window where role rename + rotator run overlapped and rotator didn't have an existence check for the grantee ARN; grant TTL expired leaving old grant referencing removed principal.

tessa: Proposed fixes: 1) add principal-existence precheck to grant-rotator and role rename pipeline; 2) make rotator create replacement grant using canonical role mapping when rename detected; 3) add a KMS-grant-monitor that alerts when grants reference non-existent principals for >2m.

ravi: Also add a unit test in infra pipeline that simulates role rename while rotator runs to catch race. Ticketing: ENG-4310 for automation changes + ENG-4311 for alerting rule.

sec-bot: Created incident stub ENG-4310 and pinned timeline. Will auto-create alert if another grant mismatch appears in next 7 days.

ops-runner: I'll run a full batch of restores in staging with the new grant-renewer flag enabled and report back. ETA 1h.

ravi: Thanks. Closing follow-up for immediate restore outage. Moving to encops backlog for automation work.
